# ethereum-optimism/op-analytics Monthly Report (June 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
June was characterized by critical validation of Interop Proofs and the identification of synchronization bottlenecks within the Superchain infrastructure. A major milestone was reached with the successful verification of the withdrawal path on the Interop Proofs Devnet, confirming that cross-chain withdrawals can be proven and finalized on a forked Sepolia network. However, development also shifted toward hardening the `op-supernode` and `op-supervisor` components, as teams diagnosed complex stalls in Consensus Layer (CL) synchronization and cross-safe backlog processing. The month concluded with a focus on infrastructure resilience, specifically addressing the deprecation of external dependencies and fixing initialization failures in the interop client.

## 🛠️ Key Developments
While no major code merges were finalized in the provided reporting period, the technical focus remained on protocol security and the stability of the Superchain's interoperability layer.

*   **Interop Proofs Validation:**
    The project successfully verified the end-to-end withdrawal path for the Interop Proofs Devnet. This work confirmed that the system can correctly generate and verify proofs for withdrawals, a foundational requirement for secure cross-chain interactions within the Superchain ecosystem.

*   **Infrastructure Maintenance:**
    In response to the announced shutdown of the Blocknative gas estimation API (scheduled for June 19, 2026), work began on transitioning the market data collection scripts (`reference_data/market_data/get_market_data.py`) to alternative data sources to ensure uninterrupted analytics reporting.

## 🐛 Issues & Triage

### Closed Issues
*   **Interop & Security:** The verification of the Interop Proofs Devnet ([#20489](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-analytics/issues/20489)) was the primary closure, marking a significant step for L2-to-L1 security. Additionally, feedback from the Lumi Security Audit regarding `doc.go` ([#21124](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-analytics/issues/21124)) was addressed, improving the project's documentation and security posture.

### New & Active Issues
*   **Supernode Synchronization Stalls:** A high-priority investigation is underway regarding `op-supernode` and `op-reth` synchronization ([#21076](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-analytics/issues/21076)). A/B testing revealed that the CL sync recovery can freeze when the Engine API encounters missing blocks, leading to timeouts and a frozen queryable state.
*   **Initialization Failures:** A new issue ([#21136](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-analytics/issues/21136)) identified a "stuck" state in the interop client. If the execution layer is unreachable at startup, the `op-supernode` fails to initialize the engine client and does not retry, necessitating a refactor of the engine-controller initialization logic.
*   **Cross-Safe Backlog Management:** Discussion continues on [#21117](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-analytics/issues/21117) regarding the inability of the `op-supervisor` to drain backlogs faster than real-time after a stall. This appears linked to sequencing window expirations, which may require manual intervention if the safe head force-increases during extended outages.

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
The month saw deep technical collaboration centered on debugging the Superchain's interoperability stack. Discussions on issues [#21076](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-analytics/issues/21076) and [#21117](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-analytics/issues/21117) indicate a high level of coordination between protocol engineers to reproduce complex edge cases involving `op-node`, `op-reth`, and the `op-supervisor`. The community's proactive response to the Blocknative API deprecation ([#1797](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-analytics/issues/1797)) demonstrates a strong commitment to maintaining the reliability of the project's data infrastructure.
